newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul gold prices slip, trade steady.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul gold prices slip, trade steady.

text.p: Trade on the Istanbul gold exchange remained steady on Wednesday with volume at 1,717 kg, compared to Tuesday's 1,789, helped by lower prices encouraging demand, dealers said.
Gold slipped to $332.60 an ounce from Tuesday's $335.00 close following 4-1/2-year lows on European markets.
Lira prices also closed easier at 1,595,500 lira per gram versus 1,597,300, the fall being cushioned by the lira weakening against the dollar.
"Lower prices seemed attractive to buyers, with physical demand coming from the Grand Bazaar. There was also a small amount of arbitrage deals by the banks," one dealer said.
Turkey's unregulated gold market is centred around Istanbul's Grand Bazaar.
The Turkish currency eased to 149,010 lira to the dollar, from Tuesday's close of 148,670.
Almost all of the day's trade -- 1,692 kg -- took place in the morning session, with 64.5 percent of the total volume conducted in lira terms.
